sentences.text:
2.  By present petition, the petitioner is seeking to quash and set aside order/communication dated 14-2-2022 issued by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Greater Mumbai with a further prayer to grant remission of three months to the petitioner in terms of Government Resolution (G.R.) dated 3-6-2017.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner was convicted on 29-11-2018 for the offences punishable under Section 376(2) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: She fairly states that benefits under the G.R. dated 3-6-2017 are available to the prisoners, who were convicted prior to 14-4-2016, the 125 th Birth Anniversary of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar.

She submits that the Government of Maharashtra has issued a clarification on 20-2-2024 stating therein that benefits under the said G.R. is also available to the prisoners, who were convicted but were released on bail on suspension of sentence pending appeal, which was filed prior to 2 cr. wp 395.2022 14-4-2016.

In support, she has relied upon Dinesh S/O Keshav Tambe vs Superintendent, Central Prison, ... on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58258247/
1 judgment of Division Bench of this Court in the case of Sonu @ Ashwin Vs. State of Maharashtra in Criminal Writ Petition No. 865/2023 dated 1-8-2024

4. That being so and since the petitioner has been convicted after the cut off date, the benefit under the G.R. will be not available to him.

By present petition, the petitioner is seeking to quash and set aside order/communication dated 14-2-2022 issued by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Greater Mumbai with a further prayer to grant remission of three months to the petitioner in terms of Government Resolution (G.R.) dated 3-6-2017.
3.
wherein the Court, after taking note of the clarification issued by the State Government, held that the G.R. was issued with a particular purpose of special remission scheme and it was made available to convicts who were in jail as on 14-4-2016 or whose appeals are/were pending but they are/were released on bail on suspension of sentence.

The petition is accordingly dismissed.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner was convicted on 29-11-2018 for the offences punishable under Section 376(2) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.
She fairly states that benefits under the G.R. dated 3-6-2017 are available to the prisoners, who were convicted prior to 14-4-2016, the 125 th Birth Anniversary of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar.
She submits that the Government of Maharashtra has issued a clarification on 20-2-2024 stating therein that benefits under the said G.R. is also available to the prisoners, who were convicted but were released on bail on suspension of sentence pending appeal, which was filed prior to 2 cr. wp 395.2022 14-4-2016.
In support, she has relied upon Dinesh S/O Keshav Tambe vs Superintendent, Central Prison, ... on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58258247/
1 judgment of Division Bench of this Court in the case of Sonu @ Ashwin Vs. State of Maharashtra in Criminal Writ Petition No. 865/2023 dated 1-8-2024
